name: SELLC StakingRewards permissionless token listing and spot-priced sell
summary: StakingRewards.addLiquidity has no access control and sets listToken[_token]=true for any caller-supplied token. sell(token, token1, amount) then pays any token1 the contract holds, priced from the caller-controlled token/token1 pair. The attacker listed its own token, created a custom pair against SellQILP (the SELLC/QIQI LP that StakingRewards held) and sold worthless tokens for the contract's LP. It burned the LP and dumped the SELLC for WBNB. Copycats repeated the drain within hours.
notes: The immutable StakingRewards runtime contains both the permissionless addLiquidity listing and the pair-quoted sell payout. Owner setup calls (updateUser, setEx) and the SellQILP balance built up from stakes do not introduce the defect, so deployment supplies the age.

Components are StakingRewards' exact net depletion in each exploit transaction: Transfer inflows minus outflows of real tokens, so attacker-supplied listing liquidity is netted. Only the first campaign is valued. Its 20712693.906761132 SellQILP (99.96% of the SELLC/QIQI pair supply was held by the victim) is valued at the attacker's realised disposal. Burning the LP yielded 6939399.227733031 SELLC and 58060083.58033396 QIQI; the SELLC plus 33689.818 SELLC the attacker bought with 3 WBNB of its own were sold into Pancake SELLC/WBNB pair 0x358efc593134f99833c66894ccecd41f550051b6 for 303.3264312585738 WBNB. Net of the 3 WBNB input that is 300.3264312585738 WBNB at the DefiLlama WBNB price. QIQI had no liquid market beyond the drained pair and is left unvalued. The pre-exploit spot value of the drained LP (about 1561 BNB of underlying at pair reserves) was not realisable against the 596.48-WBNB SELLC pool, so no spot valuation is used. Later copycat depletion (the second SellQILP, QIQI and SELLC components) is recorded without USD value; its realised proceeds were not isolated, so the USD total is a lower bound.
